treks.title: Kedarkantha Winter Trek
treks.content:
Kedarkantha is the classic first winter trek in the Himalayas. Walk through pine and oak forests, camp beside frozen lakes and finish with a sunrise summit at 12,500 ft, with 360-degree views of Swargarohini, Bandarpoonch and Black Peak.

The trail is gentle and well graded, which makes it ideal for beginners, while the snow-covered meadows and starlit camps make it a favourite with experienced trekkers too.
treks.excerpt: A beginner-friendly 6-day winter trek in Uttarakhand with snow trails, lakeside camps and a sunrise summit at 12,500 ft.

details.highlights:
Sunrise summit at 12,500 ft
Snow camping at Juda Ka Talab
Pine and oak forest trails
360-degree Himalayan panorama
Experienced certified trek leaders

details.things_to_carry:
Waterproof trekking shoes
Thermal inner wear (2 sets)
Down jacket and fleece
Waterproof gloves and woollen cap
Sunglasses, sunscreen and lip balm
20 L day pack and 1 L water bottle
Personal medicines and ID proof
details.faq: [{"q":"Is Kedarkantha suitable for beginners?","a":"Yes. It is an easy to moderate trek with gradual ascents. Reasonable fitness and some cardio practice before the trek is enough."},{"q":"Will there be snow?","a":"From mid December to March you can expect snow on most of the trail. In April the upper meadows still hold patches of snow."},{"q":"Are mobile networks available?","a":"Network is available at Sankri only. Please inform family before the trek begins."},{"q":"What is the temperature at camp?","a":"Night temperatures drop to -8 to -12 degrees Celsius in peak winter, so warm layers are essential."}]

treks.title: Triund and Indrahar Pass Trek
treks.content:
Rise above McLeod Ganj to the Triund ridge and push on to the snow line of Indrahar Pass at 14,245 ft. Pitch camp under the Dhauladhar range, with the Kangra valley glowing below you at night.

This moderate 4-day trek mixes rhododendron forests, grassy ridges and a final snow-covered climb, with views you will not forget.
treks.excerpt: A moderate 4-day Dhauladhar trek from McLeod Ganj with ridge camping and a climb to the 14,245 ft Indrahar Pass.

details.highlights:
Camp on the Triund ridge
Snow climb to Indrahar Pass
Rhododendron forest trails
Dhauladhar range panorama
Sunrise over the Kangra valley
details.exclusions:
Meals in McLeod Ganj before reporting
Personal gear rental
Travel insurance
Porter or mule charges
Any emergency evacuation cost
details.things_to_carry:
Trekking shoes with good grip
Rain jacket or poncho
Fleece and down jacket
Gloves, cap and neck gaiter
Head torch with spare batteries
Trekking pole
Water bottle (2 L total)
Personal first aid kit
details.faq: [{"q":"How difficult is Indrahar Pass?","a":"The final climb is steep and over snow, so good fitness is needed. Triund alone is much easier."},{"q":"Is camping allowed at Triund?","a":"Yes, in designated spots. We carry all camping gear and food."},{"q":"Is there drinking water on the trail?","a":"Streams near Lahesh Cave and Triund. Carry purification tablets."},{"q":"Can I leave luggage?","a":"Yes, at our McLeod Ganj base. Carry only what you need on the trek."}]
